proof:
# An exact obstruction to sharp-depth gluing of two adjacent layers

Let Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d. A plausible adjacent-layer compression would replace two equal-volume convex fibers by a source of their combined mass on the real middle plane, retaining the ordinary Gamma_d center bound. This fails even with arbitrary movement of the continuous center, with centrally symmetric rectangular fibers, and with only two fixed oblique caps. The result concerns the original two-layer measure evaluated on its real middle plane; it is not an OC counterexample.

## 1. A common-intersection lower bound

Let A,C be full-dimensional centrally symmetric convex bodies in R^d, centered at the same origin, and put them at bases 0 and 1. Write a=|A|, c=|C| and I=|A intersect C|. The mixed measure assigns ordinary d-volume to each layer. Then its depth at (1/2,0) is at least

    (min(a,c)+I)/2.                                      (1)

For a nonvertical cap through this point write its endpoint inequalities as u.x>=t and u.x>=-t. On the common body Q=A intersect C, central symmetry and boundary nullity give exactly |Q| for the sum of these two cap volumes. The two residual measures 1_(A\Q) dx and 1_(C\Q) dx are centrally symmetric, with masses a-I and c-I. At least one of t,-t is nonpositive; that residual cap therefore contains at least half its residual mass. This proves (1). A vertical cap through base 1/2 captures an entire endpoint fiber and hence at least min(a,c), which is no smaller than (1). A containing cap can be moved to pass through the point while decreasing its mass.

No claim is made that the residual supports are convex. Only their actual nonnegative symmetric measures are used.

## 2. Exact crossed rectangles

Fix 0<e<=L and d=2. Put

    A=[-L,L] times [-e,e],
    C=[-e,e] times [-L,L],
    C_body=conv(({0} times A) union ({1} times C)).

This is a full three-dimensional compact convex body, equals the convex hull of its actual mixed-integer set, and has exactly those two positive integer fibers. Both areas are

    V=4Le,

and |A intersect C|=4e^2. Write r=e/L. By (1), the depth at the real point (1/2,0,0) is at least

    B=(V+4e^2)/2=(1+r)V/2.                               (2)

The two CLOSED ambient caps

    H_+={x_2>=e-2ez},
    H_-={x_2<=-e+2ez}                                    (3)

cover the entire real middle plane z=1/2. Each intersects A only in a supporting edge of zero area. On C, each captures a rectangle of area 2e(L+e)=B. Thus every point of the entire middle plane belongs to an actual cap of mass B. Together with (2), this proves the exact all-center, all-orientation formula

    max_(x in R^2) depth_mu(1/2,x)=(1+r)V/2.              (4)

In particular no argument about differentiability, uniqueness of a mixed deepest point, or angular symmetry of optimizing caps is needed for the upper bound. The two fixed caps certify every possible moving center simultaneously.

Taking L=1,e=1/4 gives V=1 and the exact middle-plane maximum 5/8, whereas an ordinary sharp center bound for the combined mass would demand

    Gamma_2 (2V)=8/9.

More generally (4) approaches V/2 as r decreases to zero. Hence even among two equal-volume centrally symmetric planar fibers, no universal middle-plane lower bound cV with c>1/2 holds. The elementary bound V/2 from (1) is the sharp infimum in this class.

At the actual integer layers the maximal depth is exactly V/2: each own center supplies that amount, while a sufficiently steep cap isolates any prescribed own cap from the other compact fiber. This is at least the OC target Gamma_2 V. The failure is solely the proposed two-layer sharp continuous compression, not OC and not a new counter to an already rejected fixed-centroid selector.

## 3. The mass that the endpoint-only compression discards

If the same endpoint shapes are instead placed at bases -1 and 1, their actual convex hull has middle fiber

    B_0=(A+C)/2=[-(L+e)/2,(L+e)/2]^2,
    |B_0|=(L+e)^2.                                      (5)

The three-layer measure includes this new volume. Its middle origin has exact depth

    |B_0|/2+(1+r)V/2.                                    (6)

For every nonvertical cap through the origin, the middle square contributes exactly half its area, and (1) controls the endpoint pair. The two caps x_2>=-ez and x_2<=ez give the matching upper bound and cover the whole middle plane. A vertical cap has mass |B_0|+V, which exceeds (6). Since the middle-depth function is quasiconcave and invariant under x->-x, its origin maximizes it; alternatively the same two fixed caps already prove the needed global upper bound on that plane. Endpoint-layer maxima equal V/2 and are smaller than (6), so (6) is also the exact global mixed maximum in this three-layer family.

This explicitly identifies why the endpoint-only obstruction cannot be used against a gluing theorem that retains the forced Minkowski middle volume. In the thin limit |B_0|/V=(1+r)^2/(4r) tends to infinity.

All fixed cap masses, incidence inequalities, strict numerical comparisons and the three-layer formula are checked by the rational verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_two_layer_midplane_gluing_obstruction.py`. The all-cap lower bound is the elementary symmetric-measure proof in Section 1.

## 4. An asymmetric criterion that retains the actual middle body

Here the two endpoint fibers A,C can be arbitrary centrally symmetric convex bodies in R^d, with volumes 0<a<=b. An affine shear and translation put both endpoint symmetry centers at zero. Let the arbitrary middle fiber B contain D=(A+C)/2, and write

    U=|B|,  w=|D|,  I=|A intersect C|,
    K=max{b,w+a+I}/2.                                   (7)

For the actual three-fiber family at -1,0,1,

    D_max(mu)>=max{Gamma_d U,K}.                         (8)

The ordinary middle deepest point supplies Gamma_d U. The larger endpoint's own center supplies b/2. At (0,0), every proper cap takes half of the centrally symmetric subbody D from the middle fiber, and the two endpoints supply at least (a+I)/2 by Section 1. Vertical caps capture the whole middle fiber plus at least the smaller endpoint; U+a >= (w+a+I)/2 because w<=U and I<=a. Thus that point supplies (w+a+I)/2. Every stated candidate belongs to an actual fiber.

Consequently the exact sufficient condition

    max{b,w+a+I} >= 2 Gamma_d(a+b)                       (9)

implies the OC bound for this three-fiber family, for every compatible middle shape and every U. Indeed (9) says K>=Gamma_d(a+b), and

    max{Gamma_d U,K}
      >= (Gamma_d U+Gamma_d(a+b))/2.

This condition is genuinely asymmetric and retains both the forced middle volume and the common endpoint volume. It is not asserted to hold automatically. For example, in d=2 take homothetic centered squares with b=1 and a=1/4. Then I=a and w=9/16, so max{b,w+a+I}=17/16, strictly below 2Gamma_2(a+b)=10/9. Therefore these estimates alone leave a nonempty intermediate range of possible middle volumes. They do not establish the proposed induction.

For clarity, among bounds that use only (8), condition (9) is the exact threshold for settling every U>0: the function

    max{Gamma_d U,K}/(U+a+b)

has its minimum at U=K/Gamma_d, with value K/(K/Gamma_d+a+b). This equals or exceeds Gamma_d/2 precisely when K>=Gamma_d(a+b). This elementary optimization does not assert that every U or every extremal depth profile is geometrically realizable.
